title: Topology and ambient-open images of a directed quasi-affine chart limit
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, and let $U_i\subseteq Y$ be open subschemes such that $U_k\subseteq U_i$ for $i\leq k$. Assume every $U_i$ is quasi-affine, meaning a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Put $E=\bigcap_i|U_i|$ with its subspace topology and $A_i=\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_{U_i})$, with transition homomorphisms given by restriction. Let $(C,(r_i:A_i\to C)_i)$ be a colimit of this system in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $j_i:U_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ be the canonical morphism corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{A_i}$ under [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction], and put $p_i=\operatorname{Spec}(r_i):\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $Q_i=j_i(|U_i|)$. Then there is a unique continuous map $t:E\to|\operatorname{Spec}C|$ satisfying $p_i\circ t=j_i|_E$ for every $i$. It is a homeomorphism onto
$$F=\bigcap_i p_i^{-1}(Q_i),$$
and each $p_i^{-1}(Q_i)$ is a quasi-compact open of $\operatorname{Spec}C$. For every open $W\subseteq Y$ contained in $E$ and every $i\in I$, regarding $W$ as an open in $U_i$, one has
$$t(W)=p_i^{-1}(j_i(W)).$$
In particular $t(W)$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}C$; no quasi-compactness of $W$ is required.

proof.text: Write $q_{ik}=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\to A_k)$ for $i\le k$. The canonical-embedding lemma makes each $j_i$ an open immersion with quasi-compact source; thus $Q_i$ is open and quasi-compact. Naturality of the affine adjunction gives $q_{ik}j_k=j_i|_{U_k}$: both morphisms correspond to restriction $A_i\to A_k$. In particular the points $j_i(e)$ form a compatible family for every $e\in E$.

source.place: Tag 0API, lemma-sits-in-functions, proof, middle paragraph and final paragraph of cartesian squares

proof.text: Apply the filtered-spectrum topological-limit statement to the given colimit $C$. Its compatible-family homeomorphism defines a unique map $t$ by the coordinates $j_i|_E$. Each coordinate is continuous, and the spectrum topology is the coarsest making the projections continuous; therefore $t$ is continuous. The same compatible-family bijection proves uniqueness among all maps with these coordinates.

source.place: Tag 0API, lemma-sits-in-functions, proof, middle paragraph and final paragraph of cartesian squares

proof.text: Certainly $t(E)\subseteq F$. Conversely take $z\in F$ and write uniquely $p_i(z)=j_i(x_i)$ with $x_i\in U_i$, using the open embeddings. If $i\le k$, compatibility and step 1 give $j_i(x_i)=j_i(x_k)$, hence $x_i=x_k$ as points of $Y$. For arbitrary $i,l$ choose $k\ge i,l$; then $x_i=x_k=x_l$. Nonemptiness of $I$ now supplies one common point $x\in\bigcap_iU_i=E$, and coordinate uniqueness gives $z=t(x)$. The same injectivity of any $j_i$ proves injectivity of $t$.

source.place: Tag 0API, lemma-sits-in-functions, proof, middle paragraph and final paragraph of cartesian squares

proof.text: Fix $i_0\in I$. On $F$ the inverse of $t$ is $z\mapsto j_{i_0}^{-1}(p_{i_0}(z))$, regarded as a point of $E$. This map is continuous into $Y$, since $p_{i_0}(F)\subseteq Q_{i_0}$ and $j_{i_0}$ is a homeomorphism onto $Q_{i_0}$. It is continuous into the subspace $E$: the inverse image of $E\cap O$ is the inverse image of $O$ for every open $O\subseteq Y$. Thus $t:E\to F$ is a homeomorphism. The final clause of the filtered-spectrum lemma applied to the quasi-compact open $Q_i$ proves each $p_i^{-1}(Q_i)$ quasi-compact and open.

source.place: Tag 0API, lemma-sits-in-functions, proof, middle paragraph and final paragraph of cartesian squares

proof.text: Fix $i$ and an open $W\subseteq Y$ contained in $E$. For $k\ge i$, apply the affinization-square lemma to the open inclusion $U_k\subseteq U_i$, whose source and target are both quasi-affine. It identifies $q_{ik}^{-1}(j_i(U_k))$ with $j_k(U_k)$ and the restricted map with the identity on $U_k$. Since $W\subseteq U_k$, taking the inverse image of $j_i(W)$ inside this identified open gives $q_{ik}^{-1}(j_i(W))=j_k(W)$, with the same point $w\in W$ on both sides. Also $j_i(W)$ is open, because $W$ is open in $U_i$ and $j_i$ is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 0API, lemma-sits-in-functions, proof, middle paragraph and final paragraph of cartesian squares

proof.text: The coordinate identity gives $t(W)\subseteq p_i^{-1}(j_i(W))$. Conversely let $p_i(z)=j_i(w)$ with $w\in W$. For every $k\ge i$, step 5 and its identity-on-$U_k$ clause imply $p_k(z)=j_k(w)$. For arbitrary $l$ choose $k\ge i,l$; then $p_l(z)=q_{lk}p_k(z)=j_l(w)$ by step 1. Coordinate uniqueness from step 2 gives $z=t(w)$. Hence $t(W)=p_i^{-1}(j_i(W))$, an open set by continuity of $p_i$. No compactness of $W$ was used.

The item is that topological content, and its statement is unchanged; parent steps 3 and 5 use exactly the homeomorphism onto F, the qc of p_i^{-1}(Q_i) and t(W)=p_i^{-1}(j_i(W)). Checked all 6 steps against the cited statements. (1) Adjunction naturality in Z and R gives q_ik j_k=j_i|U_k; the trf embedding plus the open-immersion definition make Q_i a qc open. (2) The hypotheses of filtered-spectrum-topological-limit match the item (small, nonempty, directed, colimit in CRing); continuity comes from its coarsest-topology clause and uniqueness from its bijection. (3) Image and injectivity follow from injectivity of j_i and common upper bounds, with no affineness of intersections and no separatedness of Y assumed. (4) The inverse is j_{i0}^{-1}p_{i0}; the qc of p_i^{-1}(Q_i) comes from the node's explicit final clause. (5) The 0ARY square node is applied only to U_k⊆U_i (both quasi-affine) and never to W; its 'equivalently' clause gives q_ik^{-1}(j_i(W))=j_k(W) pointwise. (6) The elementary assembly is genuinely elementary. The item's j_i (via the adjunction) agrees with the trf node's j (via morphism-into-affine): both send f to f^sharp. Edge cases tested: constant system, empty U_i (C=0), A^2 minus 0 in A^2, D(f) in Spec B, non-qc W. No new nodes; proof_deps equals the union of uses; no cycle; the rg -L duplicate search found no other node with this statement. No SGA; tool_uses empty and none needed. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem quasiAffineChartLimitTopology (Y : Scheme.{u}) (I : Type u) [PartialOrder I] [Nonempty I] (hdir : Directed (· ≤ ·) (id : I → I)) (U : I → Y.Opens) (hU : Antitone U) [hqa : ∀ i : I, (U i).toScheme.IsQuasiAffine] (c : Cocone (quasiAffineChartSectionDiagram Y U hU)) (hc : IsColimit c) : ∃ t : C({x : Y // ∀ i : I, x ∈ U i}, Spec c.pt), (∀ (i : I) (x : {x : Y // ∀ i : I, x ∈ U i}), (Spec.map (c.ι.app i)) (t x) = (U i).toScheme.toSpecΓ ⟨x.val, x.property i⟩) ∧ (∀ t' : C({x : Y // ∀ i : I, x ∈ U i}, Spec c.pt), (∀ (i : I) (x : {x : Y // ∀ i : I, x ∈ U i}), (Spec.map (c.ι.app i)) (t' x) = (U i).toScheme.toSpecΓ ⟨x.val, x.property i⟩) → t' = t) ∧ Topology.IsEmbedding t ∧ Set.range t = ⋂ i : I, (Spec.map (c.ι.app i)) ⁻¹' Set.range (U i).toScheme.toSpecΓ ∧ (∀ i : I, IsOpen ((Spec.map (c.ι.app i)) ⁻¹' Set.range (U i).toScheme.toSpecΓ) ∧ IsCompact ((Spec.map (c.ι.app i)) ⁻¹' Set.range (U i).toScheme.toSpecΓ)) ∧ (∀ W : Y.Opens, (W : Set Y) ⊆ ⋂ i : I, (U i : Set Y) → (∀ i : I, t '' {x | x.val ∈ W} = (Spec.map (c.ι.app i)) ⁻¹' ((U i).toScheme.toSpecΓ '' {x : (U i).toScheme | x.val ∈ W})) ∧ IsOpen (t '' {x | x.val ∈ W}))
